_about: PRO rewrite pass 10: era-3 scenes 40-78 in play order.

scenarios.title: The Retirement Rumors
scenarios.text: The media have started asking how much longer you'll play: at your locker, on the radio, in a column titled 'The Last Good Years'. You're thirty-one, and you feel fine.

choices.label: Give the same answer every time
choices.result: 'As long as I'm good,' every time, to every reporter, word for word. They stop asking by October, bored, which was the point.

choices.label: Joke about the question
choices.result: A joke about needing a walker for the post-game interview. The clip goes around the league, and the columnist writes a nicer column.

choices.label: Stop answering questions
choices.result: Practice instead of interviews, every single day. Your silence says more than any answer could, and your kicks say all the rest.

scenarios.title: The Rookie's Confidence
scenarios.text: A young teammate is crumbling under online criticism after a bad game: he's stopped eating lunch with the team, and he reads the comments in the training room between treatments.

choices.label: Tell him about your worst week
choices.result: Your worst week as a pro, told to him in full, in an empty meeting room. He laughs at the worst part, which is how you know it worked.

choices.label: Take him to dinner
choices.result: Dinner, with no football talk at all: his hometown, his family, his terrible taste in music. He comes back to lunch the next day.

choices.label: Get him off the apps
choices.result: Delete them, you tell him, for one month. He does it, grudgingly, and by the end of the month he's himself again.

scenarios.title: The Former Coach's Advice
scenarios.text: An old coach, retired now, calls on a Sunday and tells you to start thinking about your next chapter. 'Not because you're done,' he says. 'Because you'll be surprised how fast it comes.'

choices.label: Make a list
choices.result: A list of things you'd want to do after football, started that night on the back of a playbook. It's longer than you expected, and some of it excites you.

choices.label: Ask him what he did
choices.result: What did he do when it ended? He tells you, over an hour, the hard parts included, and you take notes without meaning to.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.result: Not yet, you tell him, there's more kicking in you. He laughs and says that's what he said, and hangs up kindly.

scenarios.title: A Town's Thank-You
scenarios.text: Your hometown wants to honor your career with a dinner, a plaque and a key to the city, and you're still playing it. The mayor's office has already printed the invitations.

choices.label: Accept with your family beside you
choices.result: Accepted, with {parent} and {sibling} at the head table. It's a great night, and {parent} keeps the key to the city in his truck.

choices.label: Ask them to wait until you're done
choices.result: Wait until you're done, you ask kindly. They agree, a little relieved, and it gives you something to look forward to.

choices.label: Turn it into a youth clinic
choices.result: A youth clinic instead of a dinner: two hundred kids, a muddy field, and the mayor holding for you once, badly.

scenarios.title: The Guest Analyst
scenarios.text: A network offers you a guest analyst spot during your off week: a studio, a tie, a monitor full of other kickers, and a producer in your ear.

choices.label: Do it and enjoy it
choices.result: You do it, and you're good at it, explaining a kick in ways nobody has heard before. Your phone fills with texts from teammates and agents.

choices.label: Prepare like a game week
choices.result: Film of every kicker in the league, studied for three days. You say one smart thing on air, and it's the clip of the week.

choices.label: Rest during the off week
choices.result: No studio this time. It's your off week, and your body and your family come first, so the network books a punter instead.

scenarios.title: The Teammate's Contract
scenarios.text: A young teammate is in his first big negotiation and comes to your locker with the offer folded in his pocket. He wants to know what you'd do.

choices.label: Tell him what you learned
choices.result: You tell him everything you learned, including the mistakes that cost you. He takes notes on a napkin and gets a better deal than yours.

choices.label: Introduce your agent
choices.result: You introduce him to your agent over lunch. It goes well, and he thanks you in the locker room loudly enough to embarrass you both.

choices.label: Tell him to trust his agent
choices.result: You tell him to trust his agent and not to read the comments. It's good advice, and he looks like he wanted more.

scenarios.title: The Offseason Commitment
scenarios.text: Your family wants you home for the offseason; your training plan says otherwise. {parent} has already cleared out your old room, and your strength coach has already booked the gym.

choices.label: Go home and train there
choices.result: Home, with a plan: the old high school field in the mornings, family in the afternoons. Everyone's happy, including your leg.

choices.label: Stick to the plan
choices.result: The plan, followed exactly, in your training city. Home waits, and the calls are long, and your leg has never felt stronger.

choices.label: Bring them to you
choices.result: The family, flown in for a month to your training city. It's crowded and loud, and {sibling} learns to hold.

scenarios.title: The Young Kicker's Arrival
scenarios.text: A rookie kicker asks to learn your routine, step by step: the breath, the count, the spot on the ball. He's brought a notebook and a very serious face.

choices.label: Teach him everything
choices.result: Every step, and then why each step is there. He fills the notebook, and you realize, explaining it, that you understand it better too.

choices.label: Let him shadow you
choices.result: Seven days of shadowing: he does everything you do, one step behind. By Friday he's found his own version, which suits him better.

choices.label: Keep a few things yours
choices.result: Most of it, taught generously; a few things, kept. Every kicker needs a secret or two, and he'll find his own.

scenarios.title: The Team's Community Day
scenarios.text: The club asks you to organize its community day: two thousand fans, a stadium tour, a kicking contest for kids, and a budget that is mostly enthusiasm.

choices.label: Run the whole day
choices.result: Every detail, run by you, with a clipboard and a whistle. It's the best community day the club has ever had, and you lose your voice.

choices.label: Bring the players' families
choices.result: The players' families, invited to help run it. It becomes a tradition, and the kids of players teach the kids of fans to kick.

choices.label: Help where you're needed
choices.result: Help wherever you're needed, and the staff leads. It runs fine, and you spend the whole afternoon signing autographs, happily.

scenarios.title: The Family Milestone
scenarios.text: A major family occasion falls on a game weekend: {parent}'s seventieth birthday, with the whole family flying in from three states. The party is Saturday night.

choices.label: Fly in for the night
choices.result: A Friday night flight, the party, and a dawn flight back. You're exhausted at the game, and {parent} talks about your toast for years.

choices.label: Stay with the team and call
choices.result: With the team, and a long video call into the party. They put you on a laptop at the head table, and you watch {parent} blow out the candles.

choices.label: Plan a second party
choices.result: A second celebration, for the bye week, at your house. {parent} gets two birthdays this year and says it's the best one yet.

scenarios.title: The Old Teammate's Request
scenarios.text: A former teammate is starting a business and asks you to back him. He's earnest, he's prepared, and he's never run anything in his life.

choices.label: Back it with conditions
choices.result: You back it with conditions, a lawyer and a quarterly meeting. He grumbles about the paperwork and thanks you for it later.

choices.label: Back him fully
choices.result: You back him fully, because he's your friend. It's a risk, and he calls after every small win like a kid with a report card.

choices.label: Say no
choices.result: You say no, kindly. He understands, mostly, and you both pretend at the next reunion that it didn't change anything.

scenarios.title: Doubts at Thirty
scenarios.text: A slump in your thirties, and the questions are all about your age, not your form. The analysts have started using the word 'decline', and a reporter asks about retirement.

choices.label: Find the real cause in the film
choices.result: The real cause, found in the film after three nights: your plant foot, not your age. You fix it in a week and say nothing to the reporters.

choices.label: Kick two hundred a day
choices.result: Two hundred balls a day, every day, until the slump breaks. It does, on day eleven, and your leg feels every one of them.

choices.label: Lean on {holder}
choices.result: {holder}, who has seen you through everything, says simply that this is just another one. It helps more than any drill.

choices.label: Use the tools you learned
choices.result: The tools you learned the first time come right back: the breath, the word, the one thought. The slump is shorter, and the reporters move on.

scenarios.title: The Thirty-Something Streak
scenarios.text: A month without a miss, and the stories say you're better than ever at thirty-two. The highlight shows have a graphic, and the specialists have stopped saying the word.

choices.label: Stay in your routine
choices.result: Nothing changes: same breakfast, same warmup, same parking spot. You don't read a word of the stories, and the streak goes on.

choices.label: Share it with the unit
choices.result: The streak belongs to the snapper and {holder} too, and you say so in every interview. The specialists' chat is very happy.

choices.label: Enjoy it quietly at home
choices.result: A good dinner at home, the television off. You enjoy it the way you'd want to remember it, and {parent} calls to say he's proud.

scenarios.title: The Kicker They Drafted
scenarios.text: The club drafts a kicker in the middle rounds. He's watching your every kick from the sideline, taking notes, and he's very polite about it.

choices.label: Give him a show
choices.result: Every practice, a quiet show: long, clean and calm. He takes a lot of notes, and so, you notice, do the coaches.

choices.label: Teach him
choices.result: Your routine, your wind charts, your nerves: you teach him all of it. The room notices, and so does {coach}.

choices.label: Ask {coach} the plan
choices.result: The plan, asked plainly in the hallway. {coach}'s answer is honest: you're the kicker, and he's the future. Both things are true.

scenarios.title: Hurt at Thirty
scenarios.text: An injury in your thirties, a groin strain on a routine kick, and the recovery takes longer than it used to. The trainers keep saying 'at your age', gently.

choices.label: Follow the plan exactly
choices.result: The plan, exactly, for six weeks. It takes longer than it would have at twenty-five, and you come back whole.

choices.label: Push to come back
choices.result: Back two weeks early, and sore. You kick carefully for a month, and the trainers watch every rep like hawks.

choices.label: Take extra time
choices.result: Extra time, on purpose. You come back fresh and a little behind, and your body thanks you for it all season.

choices.label: Use what you learned
choices.result: What you learned last time comes straight back: the order of the exercises, the warning signs, the patience. You're back on schedule and smarter.
choices.lock_text: having been through a hard recovery before

scenarios.title: The Captain's Patch
scenarios.text: You wear the captain's patch for the first time, sewn on by the equipment manager that morning. The whole team is watching to see what a kicker does with it.

choices.label: Speak before the first game
choices.result: A speech before the first game, short and true. Your voice shakes on the second sentence, and they listen anyway, all of them.

choices.label: Thank the room
choices.result: Thanks, to every person who voted, one by one. It takes all week and it means more to them than any speech.

choices.label: Lead by example
choices.result: First on the field and last off it, every single day. You never mention the patch once, and nobody needs you to.

scenarios.title: The Holder Retires
scenarios.text: Your longtime holder retires, and the new one is half your age, a backup quarterback with soft hands and no idea how much this matters to you.

choices.label: Build trust fast
choices.result: Every spare minute, spent with the new holder: lunches, film, a hundred extra holds a day. By October the trust is there.

choices.label: Rep it out
choices.result: Holds, hundreds of them, after every practice for a month. Your leg is heavy, and the timing is perfect by the opener.

choices.label: Teach the details
choices.result: The details that took you years to learn, taught in an afternoon: the laces, the lean, the count. The new holder writes them on a wristband.

scenarios.title: The Rookie's Holdout
scenarios.text: A rookie holds out of camp over his contract, and the veterans want you to talk to him. He's twenty-two, he's scared, and his agent is very loud.

choices.label: Talk to him about the long game
choices.result: A long phone call about the long game: careers, reputations, what a room remembers. He signs a week later and thanks you.

choices.label: Stay out of his business
choices.result: His money, his business, you decide. You stay out of it, and the veterans are a little disappointed in their captain.

choices.label: Talk to his family
choices.result: His parents, worried, call you after a mutual friend gives them your number. You talk them through it, and they talk to him.

scenarios.title: The Charity Foundation Gala
scenarios.text: Your foundation holds its first gala. There are round tables, donors in suits, and a ballroom that costs more than you like to think about.

choices.label: Give the speech
choices.result: You give the speech, nervous and honest. It raises more than you hoped, and a donor finds you afterward to double their check.

choices.label: Bring the kids it helps
choices.result: You bring the kids the foundation helps and seat them at the front table. Nobody in the room forgets them, which was the point.

choices.label: Keep it small
choices.result: Small and personal: fewer tables, better food, one true story from the stage. It raises less money, and it feels completely like yours.

choices.label: Tell the story of why
choices.result: Why you started it, all of it, told to a silent ballroom. The donations double that night, and you have to sit down afterward.

scenarios.title: The Old College Friend's Wedding
scenarios.text: A college friend's wedding brings back the whole old crowd: the dorm, the band you all had, the professor everybody was afraid of. Even {best_friend} is there.

choices.label: Catch up until the lights come on
choices.result: Every old friend, caught up with, until the lights come on. {best_friend} and you close down the dance floor, badly.

choices.label: The ceremony and one dance
choices.result: The ceremony, one dance, and home before eleven. It's lovely, and you're asleep before the band plays the old song.

choices.label: Give an unplanned toast
choices.result: An unplanned toast, when the groom asks, about the night the whole dorm got snowed in. The whole room roars with laughter.

scenarios.title: The Old College Rival Retires
scenarios.text: A kicker you've competed with since college retires, in a short statement on a quiet Tuesday. You've measured yourself against him, quietly, for fifteen long years.

choices.label: Call him
choices.result: A phone call, that night. You talk for an hour about every game you shared, and he admits he always watched your kicks too.

choices.label: Say something public and kind
choices.result: Something kind, said on the record, about his long career. He thanks you the next day by text, and the league notices too.

choices.label: Sit with the news
choices.result: The news, sitting with you for a while. It's closer than it used to be, and you go for a long walk.

scenarios.title: A Kind Word From {tyler}
scenarios.text: {tyler} sends a message after a rough week for you: three misses in practice, a bad article, a coach who looked away. It's kinder than you expected.

choices.label: Call him back
choices.result: A phone call back, and an hour like old teammates. He tells you about his own worst week, and you laugh at both.

choices.label: Reply with honest thanks
choices.result: Thanks, and one honest line about the week. He replies with a thumbs-up and a photo of the two of you at seventeen.

choices.label: Read it twice
choices.result: Read twice, and kept. You don't reply right away, and the message sits in your phone, warming the whole week.

scenarios.title: The Player Rep Meeting
scenarios.text: The players' union holds a meeting about health care for retired players, in a hotel conference room. The speakers are men who played twenty years ago and can barely walk.

choices.label: Speak at the meeting
choices.result: A few words, for the players who aren't in the room anymore. The old men in the front row nod, and one of them shakes your hand for a long time.

choices.label: Learn every detail
choices.result: The details, learned and explained afterward to the young players. They listen, for once, because you're the one explaining it.

choices.label: Read the summary later
choices.result: The summary, read later at home. It's three pages, and most of it is about people you used to play with.

scenarios.title: The Players' Vote
scenarios.text: The team votes on a players-only issue, whether to boycott a sponsor's event after a bad story, and the captains want you to speak first.

choices.label: Speak first
choices.result: Short and fair, you speak first. The vote goes the way you hoped, and the young players thank you after.

choices.label: Lay out both sides
choices.result: Both sides, laid out fairly, and the decision left to them. It takes longer, and the room trusts the result more.

choices.label: Let the young players speak first
choices.result: The young players speak first, at your quiet suggestion. They're nervous and good, and the room hears some new voices.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Crisis
scenarios.text: A rookie in crisis calls you at two in the morning. He's in his car outside the facility, he's not making much sense, and he says he didn't know who else to call.

choices.label: Go to him
choices.result: Dressed and in the car in four minutes. You sit with him until the sun comes up, and you drive him home.

choices.label: Call for professional help
choices.result: You stay on the phone and call the team's counselor on the other line. They're there in twenty minutes, and so are you.

choices.label: Talk him through it
choices.result: On the phone until he's calm, and then every day after that. He never forgets it, and neither do you.

scenarios.title: The Real Estate Pitch
scenarios.text: A real estate agent with very white teeth pitches you on rental properties over lunch. The numbers look great on her tablet, and she has a building in mind.

choices.label: Study the numbers
choices.result: You take the numbers home, study them for a week and buy one small building. It's work, and it's yours.

choices.label: Ask {parent}
choices.result: You ask {parent}, who has strong opinions about landlords and stronger ones about leaky roofs. You don't buy, and you learn a lot.

choices.label: Pass on it
choices.result: You pass. You'd rather not fix anyone's sink, and the agent finds a linebacker by the end of the week.

scenarios.title: The Investment That Works
scenarios.text: An investment you made years ago, mostly to stop your advisor asking, has quietly turned into real money. Nobody knows about it but you and your advisor.

choices.label: Leave it alone
choices.result: You leave it alone and let it keep growing. It's the first time money has felt like a plan instead of a pressure.

choices.label: Share some of it
choices.result: You use some of it to clear a family debt nobody talks about. The call where you tell them is short, and nobody can speak at the end.

choices.label: Treat yourself once
choices.result: You treat yourself once, quietly: the watch you looked at for years. You wear it on game days and feel a little foolish and very happy.

scenarios.title: The Tax Audit
scenarios.text: You're audited, and every receipt from the last three years matters. A man in a gray suit wants to know about a dinner in 2023 that you don't remember at all.

choices.label: Hire an accountant
choices.result: A good accountant, hired that same afternoon. It's expensive and calm, and the man in the gray suit leaves satisfied.

choices.label: Do it yourself
choices.result: Every receipt, organized by you, every night for a month. You learn a great deal about your own life, some of it embarrassing.

choices.label: Sort receipts with {parent}
choices.result: {parent}, at the kitchen table, sorting receipts into shoeboxes with you for a week. He finds the 2023 dinner receipt in a coat pocket.

scenarios.title: The Charity Scam
scenarios.text: A charity using your name and photo turns out to be a scam. Families donated believing you were behind it, and a reporter has called your agent for a comment.

choices.label: Go to the authorities
choices.result: The authorities, called that same day, and a public statement in plain words. The scam shuts down within a week.

choices.label: Make the families whole
choices.result: The families who were fooled, repaid from your own pocket, quietly. One of them writes you a letter you keep forever.

choices.label: Let your lawyer handle it
choices.result: Your lawyer handles all of it. It takes a year, and the story keeps your name attached the whole time.

scenarios.title: The Bad Sponsor
scenarios.text: A sponsor is in the news for the wrong reasons: a factory scandal, a recall, a CEO in handcuffs. Your face is on its billboards in four cities.

choices.label: End the deal publicly
choices.result: The deal, ended the same day, with a short statement explaining why. Fans respect it, and your agent finds a better sponsor within a month.

choices.label: Talk to the sponsor first
choices.result: A private call to the sponsor first, before any statement. They pull the ads themselves, and you part on decent terms, mostly.

choices.label: Ride it out
choices.result: Riding it out, saying nothing at all. It costs you some fans and a lot of uncomfortable questions at your locker every week.

scenarios.title: The Public Speaking Gig
scenarios.text: A company wants you to give a motivational talk to two thousand employees in a convention center. The fee is large, and the topic is 'resilience'.

choices.label: Give a real talk
choices.result: A real talk, about failing in public and staying. They stand up at the end, and three people find you afterward to tell their own stories.

choices.label: Tell stories and laugh
choices.result: Funny stories, mostly about your own mistakes. They laugh a lot, and the CEO asks you back for next year.

choices.label: Turn the speech down
choices.result: Speeches aren't your thing, you decide, and you turn it down politely. They book an astronaut instead, who is much better.

scenarios.title: The Kids' Book
scenarios.text: A publisher wants you to write a children's book about learning to kick. The editor says to write it the way you'd tell it to a seven-year-old.

choices.label: Write it
choices.result: You write it at the kitchen table with your kids correcting every page. The dedication is to them, and they read it to their classes.

choices.label: Write it with {holder}
choices.result: You write it with {holder}, who insists on a chapter about the holder. It's funnier than the one you'd have written alone.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.result: You pass for now and tell the editor maybe after football. You keep the email, and some nights you start a first line in your head.

scenarios.title: The Hometown Field
scenarios.text: Your hometown is naming the youth field after you, the one with the crooked goalpost where you learned to kick. The ceremony is in June.

choices.label: Bring the family
choices.result: You bring the whole family. {parent} stands under the sign for a long time without saying anything, then asks someone to take the picture again.

choices.label: Kick the first ball
choices.result: You kick the first ball with the youth league. It hits the crooked post, the kids scream, and it's the best thing that happens all summer.

choices.label: Keep it quiet
choices.result: Small, please: no speeches, just the sign. Afterward you walk the field alone and find your old spot by the fence.

scenarios.title: The High School Visit
scenarios.text: You visit your old high school for an assembly. The kicking net is still behind the bleachers, the hole you kicked in the fence was never fixed, and the coach is still there.

choices.label: Kick with the team
choices.result: Kicks with the current team on their practice field, for an hour. Their kicker can't believe it, and neither can his coach.

choices.label: Find your old coach
choices.result: Your old coach, found in the weight room, gray now. You talk for an hour, and he shows you the fence.

choices.label: Stand by the net
choices.result: A while by the old net, alone. You think about the kid who kicked there, and how much he wanted this.

scenarios.title: The Kicker You Mentored
scenarios.text: A kicker you spent two summers mentoring signs with a rival club, the one you play twice a year. He sends you a picture of his new locker.

choices.label: Congratulate him
choices.result: You congratulate him first, before the news breaks. He tells a reporter he learned everything from you, and you pretend not to be moved.

choices.label: Raise your game
choices.result: You raise your game. Twice a year you'll be on the same field, and you're not letting him outkick his teacher.

choices.label: Watch him play
choices.result: His first game for the rival, watched from your couch with a bowl of popcorn. You smile at every warmup kick that looks exactly like yours.

scenarios.title: The New Special Teams Unit
scenarios.text: Half your special teams unit is new this season: a new snapper, two new wings, a holder who has never held in a real game. The timing is all wrong.

choices.label: Teach the new ones
choices.result: You teach the new ones everything you know, from the cadence to the jokes. By October the unit sounds like a unit.

choices.label: Build the unit
choices.result: You take the unit to dinner every Thursday. The timing comes after the trust, which is how it always works.

choices.label: Rep it out
choices.result: You rep it out after every practice until the timing is right. Your leg is tired, and the operation is clean.

scenarios.title: The Coordinator's Trick Plays
scenarios.text: The coordinator wants more fakes and more onside kicks this year, with you running half of them. He's drawn eleven new trick plays, and one involves you throwing.

choices.label: Master them
choices.result: Every trick play, mastered over a month of extra sessions. The coordinator starts calling you his secret weapon, which worries you a little.

choices.label: Pick the best ones
choices.result: The best three, picked with him over coffee, and you talk him out of the rest. He thanks you later, after the fourth one fails in practice.

choices.label: Get the unit excited
choices.result: The whole unit, fired up about the trick plays. Practice is fun again, and {holder} insists on running the one where you throw.

scenarios.title: The Veteran Day Off
scenarios.text: The club gives veterans a day off each week, and you're now one of them. The first Wednesday, you show up anyway out of habit, and the security guard laughs.

choices.label: Take the day off
choices.result: The day off, taken, every single week. Your legs thank you, and you start learning to cook on Wednesday afternoons.

choices.label: Come in anyway
choices.result: In anyway, for light work and film. The young players notice your car in the lot, for better and for worse.

choices.label: Spend it at home
choices.result: Wednesdays at home: school runs, long lunches, a nap on the couch. It quickly becomes the best part of your week.

scenarios.title: The Body Maintenance Plan
scenarios.text: A trainer builds you a maintenance plan for the next five years: a thick binder, color-coded, with your age printed in the header of every single page.

choices.label: Follow it
choices.result: Followed to the letter, every page. It's dull, and your leg feels five years younger by the end of the season.

choices.label: Add to it
choices.result: The plan, plus your own work on top. You're stronger and more tired, and the trainer adds a page about rest.

choices.label: Do half
choices.result: Half the binder, and the rest of your life. The trainer sighs, accepts it, and adds a page titled 'compromise'.
